sections.h2: What the Grady County Clerk does
sections.html:
The Grady County Clerk is the county's recorder. The office files warranty deeds, mortgages and oil and gas leases, and it also runs county accounts payable, employee pay and purchasing. After a home sale closes, the deed ends up here. Until it is recorded, the public record still shows the old owner.

Land records are computerized from 1929 to the present. You can search them online at OKCountyRecords.com, though fees apply there. The courthouse in Chickasha is itself on the National Register of Historic Places.

Recording a conforming document costs $18 for the first page and $2 for each page after that. The $18 is $8 for recording plus a $10 preservation fee.

Grady County Clerk fees
Filing or serviceFee
First page, conforming document$18 ($8 plus $10 preservation)
Each additional page$2
First page, non-conforming document$25, plus $10 preservation
Each additional page, non-conforming$10
Copy$1 per page
Certified copy$1 per document
Documentary stamps$1.50 per $1,000

The office takes cash and checks if you give a correct address and a current phone number. It does not take temporary checks.

A conforming page has a 2-inch margin at the top, 1-inch margins on the other three sides, and dark, legible print. A page that fails the test moves from $18 to $25 on page one and from $2 to $10 on each added page.

Two more filing rules catch sellers off guard:

  • The clerk needs a notarized original with original signatures, or a certified copy of an original.
  • A certified copy is stamped and sealed, and nothing can be added to it and refiled.

A title company that prepares your deed normally handles the format. Owners who draft their own deed for a family transfer or a quick sale are the ones most likely to pay the higher rate.

Stamps are due on any deed where money or other consideration changes hands. The clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars of price, and a chart in the office shows common amounts.

That rate equals the state's. Under 68 O.S. 3201 the tax is 75 cents for each $500 of consideration, or any fractional part, when the amount is more than $100, and it reaches only conveyances of realty that are sold. Every instrument filed must either pay the stamps or show its exemption on its face.

The clerk recommends attaching a bill of sale or a contract as proof of the price.

sections.h2: How fast a document is filed
sections.html:
A document delivered between 8 am and 4 pm is filed that day. Anything presented after 4 pm is filed the next day. Getting the document back takes seven to ten days.

The office scans every document and does not keep the original. Because of storage limits it stopped making shelf books at Book 4000, but all images are held online and backed up two ways. If you need the document right away, ask for a certified copy once it is filed, or use the online index.

  • Bring the full legal description.
  • Bring the closing statement for the stamp calculation.
  • Ask whether a DD-214 discharge record needs filing in the same visit, since the clerk's office files those too.

DD-214 records are not public. Only the service member, a spouse, children, the VA or a court order can open them.

A cash sale follows the same recording path as any other sale, with fewer lender steps ahead of it. Once buyer and seller sign, the deed goes to the clerk with proof of price and payment of the stamps.

  1. Confirm the legal description against your last recorded deed.
  2. Sign the deed in front of a notary, since the clerk needs a notarized original.
  3. Attach a closing statement, bill of sale or contract as proof of price.
  4. Work out documentary stamps at $1.50 per thousand, or state the exemption on the deed.
  5. Deliver the deed by 4 pm to have it filed the same day.

Many Grady County deeds describe ranch or farm tracts. Those descriptions run longer than a town lot and can push a deed past one page, which adds $2 for each extra page.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Walk in with a short stack and the visit goes quickly. You want the signed, notarized original deed, the closing statement or contract that shows the price, a payment that matches the page count, and a correct return address and phone number. Add a bill of sale if the price is not on the closing statement. If you are filing a mortgage or an oil and gas lease along with the deed, keep each document separate, since the fee is figured per document.

Ask the clerk to confirm the page count before you pay. A deed that runs to a second page costs $2 more, or $10 more if the format fails, and it is easier to fix a margin at the counter than after the document is accepted.

sections.h2: Reading the record on older farm land
sections.html:
Grady County was organized in 1907. Before statehood, most of it belonged to the Chickasaw Nation, and the 1898 Curtis Act began the allotment process that turned communal land into individual parcels. Those allotments are the start of many deed chains here.

That history matters when you list a farm or ranch tract. A title search may run back to an allottee, and the description may refer to a quarter section instead of a lot and block. Check your description against the last recorded deed before the new one is typed, and keep the closing statement ready for the stamp calculation.

Make sure the legal description on the deed matches the one in your last recorded deed. A typo can mean a corrective deed and a second recording fee. Many sales here involve older houses and acreage, with a median build year of 1981, so confirm that your own deed was recorded before you sell. Fixing any gap before closing speeds things up.

Property tax is a separate office. The Grady County Treasurer collects it, so request the balance there before the closing date.

Old farm deeds can trace back to Chickasaw allotments, so a title search on an older tract may run back to an allottee rather than a land patent. If the chain looks broken, tell your title company early. Towns like Chickasha, Minco, Verden, Rush Springs and Tuttle each turn up in deed descriptions, and the clerk's online index can be searched to see how your property was described the last time it changed hands.

faqs.q: How much does the Grady County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $18 for the first page and $2 for each additional page, which includes an $8 recording fee and a $10 preservation fee. A non-conforming document costs $25 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus the $10 preservation fee.

faqs.q: What is the documentary stamp rate in Grady County?
faqs.a: The clerk charges $1.50 per thousand dollars of consideration, equal to 75 cents per $500 under 68 O.S. 3201. It applies when the price is more than $100, and every deed must pay it or state its exemption.

faqs.q: Can I record a copy of a deed in Grady County?
faqs.a: Only a notarized original with original signatures, or a certified copy of an original, can be filed. A plain photocopy is not accepted.

faqs.q: How long until I get my recorded deed back?
faqs.a: Expect seven to ten days. Documents delivered by 4 pm are filed that day, and later ones are filed the next day.

faqs.q: What does a copy of a recorded document cost in Grady County?
faqs.a: A plain copy is $1 per page, and a certified copy is $1 per document.
